children.translated_text: <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen to the origin of that <s>Sāvarṇi</s>, son of the Sun,
who is spoken of as the eighth Manu, as I relate it in detail.
By the power of <s>Mahāmāyā</s> (the Great Illusion),
that fortunate son of the Sun, <s>Sāvarṇi</s>, became the lord of a manvantara.
Formerly, in the interval of <s>Svārociṣa</s>, born from the line of <s>Caitra</s>,
there was a king named <s>Suratha</s> over the whole circle of the earth.

children.text: tasya pālayataḥ samyak prajāḥ putrān ivaurasān
children.translated_text: While he was properly protecting his subjects like his own bodily sons,
enemy kings, the destroyers of the <s>Kolā</s>, arose against him then.
He, whose power of punishment was exceedingly strong, had a war with them;
although they were fewer, he was defeated in battle by those destroyers of the <s>Kolā</s>.
Then he returned to his own city and remained lord of his own country,
but that great-souled one was then beset by those powerful enemies.
There, even in his own city, his treasury and army were seized

children.text: kośo balaṃ cāpahṛtaṃ tatrāpi svapure tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: by powerful, wicked, evil-minded ministers while he was weak.
Then that king, his sovereignty taken away, under the pretext of hunting,
mounted a horse alone and went into a dense forest.
There he saw the hermitage of the excellent twice-born sage <s>Medhas</s>,
filled with peaceful wild animals and adorned by the sage's disciples.

children.text: tasthau kañcit sa kālaṃ ca muninā tena satkṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Honored by that sage, he stayed there for some time,
wandering here and there in that hermitage of the excellent muni.
There, with his mind drawn by possessive attachment, he thought:

children.text: matpūrvaiḥ pālitaṃ pūrvaṃ mayā hīnaṃ puraṃ hi tat
children.translated_text: 'That city, formerly protected by my ancestors and now bereft of me,
is it being governed according to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) by those servants of mine with bad conduct, or not?

children.text: na jāne sa pradhāno me śūrahastī sadāmadaḥ
children.translated_text: I do not know what enjoyments my chief elephant,
heroic and always in rut, will obtain now that he has fallen under the power of my enemies.
Those who were always my followers through favor, wealth, and food,
surely today they are serving other kings.
With those men of improper spending habits constantly making expenditures,
that treasury, accumulated with great difficulty, will go to ruin.'
The king constantly pondered this and other such matters.
There, near the Brahmin's hermitage, he saw a certain merchant.

children.text: sa pṛṣṭastena kastvaṃ bho hetuścāgamane 'tra kaḥ
children.translated_text: He asked him, 'Who are you, sir, and what is the reason for your coming here?

children.text: saśoka iva kasmāttvaṃ durmanā iva lakṣyase ||
children.translated_text: Why do you appear sorrowful, as if downcast?'
Hearing the king's words, spoken with affection,

children.text: pratyuvāca sa taṃ vaiśyaḥ praśrayāvanato nṛpam ||
children.translated_text: that merchant, bowing humbly, answered the king.
The merchant said:
'I am a merchant named <s>Samādhi</s>, born in a wealthy family.
I have been cast out by wicked sons and wife because of their greed for wealth.
Bereft of wealth, wife, and sons, after they took my wealth,
I have come to the forest in sorrow, rejected by trusted relatives.
Staying here, I do not know the welfare or misfortune

children.text: pravṛttiṃ svajanānāṃ ca dārāṇāṃ cātra saṃsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of my sons, of my own people, or of my wife.

children.text: kiṃ nu teṣāṃ gṛhe kṣemamakṣemaṃ kiṃ nu sāmpratam
children.translated_text: Is there well-being in their house now, or is there distress?

children.text: kathaṃ te kiṃ nu sadvṛttā durvṛttāḥ kiṃ nu me sutāḥ ||
children.translated_text: How are they? Are my sons well-conducted, or ill-conducted?'
The king said:
'Those greedy sons, wife, and others have rejected you for your wealth.
Why does your mind still cling to affection for them?'
The merchant said:
'It is just as you have said, my lord, regarding my situation.

children.text: kiṃ karomi na badhnāti mama niṣṭhuratāṃ manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What can I do? My mind does not take on harshness.
They abandoned a father's affection and rejected me, greedy for wealth;

children.text: patiḥ svajanahārdaṃ ca hādirteṣveva me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: yet my mind has affection precisely for them, for wife and kin.
I do not understand what this is, though I know it, O very wise one:
the mind inclines to love even toward relatives without virtue.

children.text: teṣāṃ kṛte me niḥśvāso daurmanasyaṃ ca jāyate
children.translated_text: For their sake my sighing and dejection arise.
What can I do, since my mind is not harsh toward them though they feel no affection?'
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: tatastau sahitau vipra taṃ muniṃ samupasthitau
children.translated_text: Then the two together, O Brahmin, approached that sage:
that merchant named <s>Samādhi</s> and that best of kings.

children.text: kṛtvā tu tau yathānyāyaṃ yathārhaṃ tena saṃvidam
children.translated_text: Having duly, and as was fitting, conversed with him,
the merchant and the king sat down and held some discussion.
The king said:
'Blessed sir, I wish to ask you one thing; please tell me this.
My mind is subject to sorrow, though it is under my own control.
Although my kingdom is gone, I still have possessive attachment to all the limbs of the kingdom.
Knowing this, yet like an ignorant man, what is this, O best of sages?
And this man, deceived by his sons, abandoned by wife and servants,
and forsaken by his own people, nevertheless has deep affection for them.
Thus both he and I are exceedingly afflicted,
our minds drawn by possessive attachment even toward objects whose faults we see.
What is this, O greatly fortunate one, that delusion occurs even in those who know,
this foolishness of one blinded in discrimination, in me and in him?'
The seer said:
'Every creature has knowledge in the sphere of sense objects,
and sense objects, O greatly fortunate one, are apprehended in this way, each separately.
Some creatures are blind by day, and others are likewise blind at night;
some creatures see equally by day and by night.

children.text: jñānino manujāḥ satyaṃ kintu te na hi kevalam
children.translated_text: Human beings are indeed knowers, but they are not the only ones;
for all beings are knowers, including cattle, birds, deer, and the rest.
And the knowledge that belongs to human beings is also that which belongs to those deer and birds.'
And whatever else belongs equally to those human beings and to both of them, it is the same.
Even though they possess knowledge, see these birds,
out of delusion eager to drop grains into their fledglings' beaks, though themselves afflicted by hunger.
Human beings too, tiger among men, are full of longing for their sons,

children.text: lobhāt pratyupakārāya nanvetān kiṃ na paśyasi ||
children.translated_text: out of greed for return-benefit. Do you not see these people?
Even so, they have been cast into the whirlpool of possessiveness, into the pit of delusion,
by the power of <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, which causes the continuance of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Therefore no wonder should be felt here: she is the yogic sleep of the Lord of the world,
this <s>Mahāmāyā</s> of <s>Hari</s>; by her the world is deluded.

children.text: jñānināmapi cetāṃsi devī bhagavatī hi sā
children.translated_text: For she, the blessed goddess, even seizes the minds of the wise,
drawing them by force, and <s>Mahāmāyā</s> hands them over to delusion.
By her this universe is sent forth, this world with its moving and unmoving beings;

children.text: saiṣā prasannā varadā nṛṇāṃ bhavati muktaye ||
children.translated_text: when she is gracious, she becomes a giver of boons to human beings for liberation.
She is the supreme knowledge, eternal, being the cause of liberation,
and she herself is also the cause of bondage in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the mistress of the lord of all.
The king said:

children.text: bhagavan kā hi sā devī mahāmāyeti yāṃ bhavān
children.translated_text: Blessed sir, who indeed is that goddess whom you call <s>Mahāmāyā</s>?

children.text: bravīti kathamutpannā sā karmāsyāśca kiṃ dvija ||
children.translated_text: How was she born, and what is her action, O twice-born one?

children.text: yatsvabhāvā ca sā devī yatsvarūpā yadudbhavā
children.translated_text: What is the nature of that goddess, what is her form, and from what did she arise?

children.text: tat sarvaṃ śrotumicchāmi tvatto brahmavidāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear all this from you, best of knowers of <s>brahman</s>.
The seer said:
She is eternal, the very form of the world; all this is pervaded by her.
Yet her manifestation is heard of in many ways; listen to it from me.
When she appears for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose,
then, though eternal, she is called 'born' in the world.
When <s>Viṣṇu</s>, at the end of an age, while the world had become a single ocean,
spread out <s>Śeṣa</s> and entered yogic sleep, the blessed Lord,
then two terrible asuras, famous as <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>,
born from the wax of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s ears, set out to kill <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: sa nābhikamale viṣṇoḥ sthito brahmā prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of creatures, was standing on the lotus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s navel;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tāvasurau cograu prasuptaṃ ca janārdanam ||
children.translated_text: seeing those two fierce asuras and <s>Janārdana</s> asleep,
with concentrated heart he praised that <s>Yoganidrā</s>,
who had made her abode in <s>Hari</s>'s eyes, for the awakening of <s>Hari</s>.
The lord praised her as mistress of the universe, bearer of the world, maker of preservation and destruction,
the blessed sleep of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, incomparable in splendor.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tvaṃ hi vaṣaṭkāraḥ svarātmikā
children.translated_text: You are <s>svāhā</s>, you are <s>svadhā</s>, and you are the <s>vaṣaṭ</s>-utterance, whose essence is the sacred tone.
You are nectar; in the imperishable, eternal syllable you abide as the three measures.
You are the eternal half-measure, especially that which is not pronounced;

children.text: tvameva saṃdhyā sāvitrī tvaṃ vedajananī parā ||
children.translated_text: you alone are twilight, <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the supreme mother of the Veda.
By you this universe is upheld; by you this world is created;

children.text: tvayaitat pālyate devi tvamatsyante ca sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: by you this is protected, O goddess, and you always consume it at the end.

children.text: visṛṣṭau sṛṣṭirūpā tvaṃ sthitirūpā ca pālane
children.translated_text: At creation you are creation-form; in preservation you are preservation-form;
and at the end you are destruction-form of this world, O you whose form is the world.
You are great knowledge, great illusion, great intelligence, great memory,
and great delusion; you are the great goddess, the great asurī.
You are <s>prakṛti</s> of all, manifesting the three <s>guṇas</s>;
you are the night of time, the great night, and the terrible night of delusion.
You are fortune, you are sovereignty, you are modesty; you are understanding, marked by awakening;

children.text: lajjā puṣṭistathā tuṣṭistvaṃ śāntiḥ kṣāntireva ca ||
children.translated_text: you are shame, nourishment, and satisfaction; you are peace and forbearance as well.

children.text: khaḍginī śūlinī ghorā gadinī cakriṇī tathā
children.translated_text: You bear sword and spear, are terrible, bear mace and discus too,
and bear conch, bow, arrows, sling, and iron club as weapons.
You are gentle, more gentle than all that is gentle, and exceedingly beautiful;
of things higher and lower, you alone are the highest, the supreme mistress.
Whatever object exists anywhere, whether real or unreal, O you whose self is all,

children.text: tasya sarvasya yā śaktiḥ sā tvaṃ kiṃ stūyase mayā ||
children.translated_text: the power of all of that is you. How can I praise you?

children.text: yayā tvayā jagatsraṣṭā jagatpātātti yo jagat
children.translated_text: Even he by whom, as you, the world is created, and by whom the world is protected and eaten,
has been brought under the sway of sleep; what lord here is able to praise you?
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, I myself, and <s>Īśāna</s> too

children.text: kāritāste yato 'tastvāṃ kaḥ stotuṃ śaktimān bhavet ||
children.translated_text: have been made by you to assume bodies; therefore who could be powerful enough to praise you?
So, O goddess, praised in this way for your own noble powers,
delude these two hard-to-subdue asuras, <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>.
Let <s>Acyuta</s>, the lord of the world, quickly be brought to awakening,
and let understanding be produced in him so that he may kill these two great asuras.
The seer said:

children.text: evaṃ stutā tadā devī tāmasī tatra vedhasā
children.translated_text: Thus praised then by <s>Vedhas</s>, the dark goddess there,
for the awakening of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and for the destruction of <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>,
came forth from his eyes, mouth, nostrils, arms, heart,
and breast, and stood visible before <s>Brahmā</s>, the one of unmanifest birth.
Then <s>Janārdana</s>, lord of the world, released by her, arose
from his serpent-couch in the single ocean; then he saw those two,
<s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, wicked, very powerful and valiant,
their eyes red with anger, prepared to devour <s>Brahmā</s>.
Then the blessed <s>Hari</s>, having risen, fought with those two,
the all-pervading one using his arms as weapons, for five thousand years.
Those two also, maddened by excessive strength and deluded by <s>Mahāmāyā</s>,
said to <s>Keśava</s>, 'Choose a boon from us.'
The blessed Lord said:
If you are pleased with me today, both of you must be slain by me.
What need is there of any other boon here? This much indeed has been chosen by me.
The seer said:
Then, deceived by the two in this way, the whole world being made of water...
Having seen this, the lotus-eyed Blessed One was addressed by those two:

children.text: āvāṃ jahi na yatrorvī salilena pariplutā ||
children.translated_text: "Slay us where the earth is not flooded over with water."
The seer said:
Saying "So be it," the Blessed One, bearer of conch, discus, and mace,

children.text: kṛtvā cakreṇa vai chinne jaghane śirasī tayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: placed them upon his thigh and cut off both their heads with his discus.
Thus she herself arose, praised by <s>Brahma</s>;

children.text: prabhāvamasyā devyāstu bhūyaḥ śṛṇu vadāmi te ||
children.translated_text: now listen again, and I shall tell you the power of this goddess.
